comparison: Perfect alignment on genome size validation (C22-C24, C74-C75). Both evaluations support the methodological approach with complete claim overlap. OpenEval emphasizes statistical evidence and quality filtering, while peer review highlights the use of C-values to mitigate assembly biases.

Strong agreement on the main negative finding (C8, C40-C41, C47, C72, C120). Both evaluations support the null result that effective population size does not correlate with TE content/genome size. OpenEval notes adequate statistical power with 807 species; peer reviewers describe this as 'convincing' and the study's primary contribution.

Both support the TE-genome size correlation (C25-C30, C6, C77-C79). OpenEval provides detailed statistical validation with adjusted-R² values and notes the avian exception. Peer reviewers accept this as foundational, emphasizing the comprehensive pipeline and phylogenetic diversity as strengths.

Both support dN/dS validation as Nee proxy (C35-C39, C92-C93). OpenEval emphasizes concordance between methods and PIC analysis rigor. Peer reviewers accept this methodological approach without challenge, treating dN/dS and life history traits as reliable proxies.

Both support the main conclusion about lineage-specific effects (C10, C73, C123). OpenEval notes the conclusion is well-supported despite weak clade-specific patterns. Peer reviewers accept that no simple global hypothesis explains variation, emphasizing lineage-specific host-TE conflicts.

Divergent evaluations of clade-specific patterns (C42-C53, C9). OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN due to weak effect sizes (adjusted-R² 0.004-0.063) and lack of multiple testing correction. Peer reviewers rate as SUPPORTED, accepting heterogeneous patterns without challenging statistical robustness. Peer review also includes Coevol results (C58, C102-C106) not in OpenEval R5.

Both support the importance of phylogenetic correction (C94, C97, C99). OpenEval emphasizes how uncorrected analyses yield artifactual results while PIC analyses avoid confounding. Peer reviewers highlight phylogenetic nonindependence accounting as a key strength making results 'highly convincing.'

Both support TE annotation methodology (C82-C83). OpenEval notes adequate validation with EarlGrey comparison and appropriate acknowledgment of limitations. Peer reviewer initially raised concerns but accepted the approach after revision, stating concerns were 'sufficiently acknowledged and addressed.'

Partial overlap on clade-specific Coevol patterns (C102-C106, C58). OpenEval supports these findings as more convincing than weak dN/dS correlations, noting mammalian and fish patterns corroborate prior work. Peer review R4 accepts clade-specific findings broadly without detailed evaluation of Coevol vs PIC methods.

Minimal overlap on avian exception (C26). OpenEval notes the avian exception to TE-genome size correlation as appropriately documented. Peer reviewer acknowledges birds as 'weird' exception, accepting the deviation without challenge.

OpenEval evaluates TE age correlations (C61-C71) as UNCERTAIN due to weak effect sizes (1.2% variance), contradictory results between methods, and uniform 5% divergence threshold issues. No corresponding peer review evaluation found.

OpenEval supports the sensitivity analysis ruling out genome duplication as confounding factor (C48-C49, C84-C85), showing TEs explain far more variance. No corresponding peer review evaluation found.

OpenEval supports methodological rigor and theoretical justification for dN/dS as long-term Nee proxy (C88-C91), distinguishing from short-term polymorphism-based estimates. No corresponding peer review evaluation found.

OpenEval supports acknowledgment of phylogenetic scale limitations (C117-C119), noting insects/molluscs are more ancient than mammals/birds, limiting comparability. No corresponding peer review evaluation found.

OpenEval supports theoretical context explaining why MHH assumptions may not apply to TEs (C125-C130), noting TEs deviate from neutral mutation assumptions. No corresponding peer review evaluation found.

OpenEval supports temporal scale hypothesis reconciling short-term vs long-term Nee patterns (C137-C140), providing framework for understanding contradictions with prior work. No corresponding peer review evaluation found.
